name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Bill Foster holds a massive financial edge: $2.5 million cash on hand versus about $23,000 for Jeff Walter
District leans Democratic by six points on the partisan lean, and the national environment adds to the Democratic side
Prediction markets price Foster at roughly 96% to win

model.rationale: Foster combines a Democratic-leaning seat, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage, while markets price him near certain to win. With no polls or contrary evidence available, the fundamentals-based estimate of a high-teens Democratic margin stands essentially unchanged.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race, or significant outside spending against Foster, would be the first sign the margin is narrower than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans Democratic by about six points. He has raised more than $2.1 million and holds roughly $2.5 million on hand, while Republican challenger Jeff Walter has raised about $311,000 with only about $23,000 remaining. No outside groups are reported spending in the race.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Foster roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money gap. The forecast expects Foster to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive race.
